deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 19% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 35% last year; 13%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 18% (3 years ago 7%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $18 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 21% (3 years ago 8%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $2.5B, up 25% from a year ago — about 42% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $311M, up 12% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 13%/yr over 3 years and 12%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 12% vs a 5-year range of 4–14% (median 7%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $422M to shareholders over the last 12 months ($422M buybacks + $0M dividends) = 1.1% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.0% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $10.33, up 29% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $7.17, up 10% in 90 days; 18 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +215% vs a year ago · $4.48 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 215% vs sales 37% (latest quarter vs a year earlier): profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 5 quarters running, by growing margins (11% → 17%): analysts keep underestimating it.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +37% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $6.0B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 37% vs a year earlier and speeding up (from 33% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $12 of operating profit, up from $5 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 124% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 58× last year's profit (higher than 57% of the last 5 years); only 23× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Dec 10; analysts expect EPS of $2.08, up 128% from a year ago. It usually moves about 13% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.
